items.title: Brotli / Node.js Vulnerabilities
items.summary: On October 22, 2026, Open AI security researchers announced a critical severity vulnerability in Google’s Brotli decoder, identified as CVE-2026-111497.

items.title: What’s new for GeoAI in the ArcGIS Pro 3.8 Image Analyst extension
items.summary: The ArcGIS Pro 3.8 release introduces several enhancements to the GeoAI capabilities in the Image Analyst extension.

items.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability
items.summary: On November 17, 2026, details emerged exposing a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in OpenJDK, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (dubbed “Java4Shell”) with a CVSSv3.1 score of 8.1 (High).

items.title: What's new in ArcGIS Linear Referencing: November 2026
items.summary: Starting with ArcGIS Pro 3.8 and ArcGIS Enterprise 12.2, ArcGIS Roads and Highways and ArcGIS Pipeline Referencing come together in a single extension: ArcGIS Linear Referencing.

items.title: Take accessible PDFs further with ArcGIS Pro 3.8
items.summary: If you ’ve only got 1 minute to be wow ed by all the new accessible PDF features we’ve added in ArcGIS Pro 3.8, check out this video .

items.title: Why U.S. Islands Are Important for Biodiversity
items.summary: Along with the more well-known islands like the Aleutian and Hawaiian Islands, the United States is home to thousands of islands found much closer to the mainland, scattered along coastlines, tucked inside estuaries, and forming barrier islands that separate coastal wetlands from the open ocean .

items.title: Opinion | America’s AI policy has a chip-size hole in it
items.summary: # America’s AI policy has a chip-size hole in it The Nvidia scandal exposed the limits of export controls. Washington needs a plan to enforce them.

items.title: NGA AI Plan: Federal Frontier Models, State Rules
items.summary: On November 22, 2026, the National Governors Association (NGA) published bipartisan principles that split AI governance between Washington and the states: the federal government should oversee frontier models, critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, and international AI, while states keep authority over consumers, workers, children, privacy, and how AI is deployed in daily life.

items.title: AG Letitia James announces a unit to police AI companies before New York’s AI safety law kicks in January 1
items.summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced a new unit on November 17 to enforce the state’s artificial intelligence laws, six weeks before the Responsible AI Safety and Education Act takes effect January 1, 2027.

items.title: Wall Street Hit by 'AI Skepticism'... "Data Centers, China Export Controls" Two Major Headwinds (Roundup)
items.summary: A pessimistic outlook has emerged that skepticism over artificial intelligence (AI) investment could lead to the collapse of the so-called “Techno-Dollar” system.

items.title: Australian AI Safety Standard: Enterprise LLM Playbook
items.summary: Australian enterprises deploying large language models must align governance controls with the Voluntary AI Safety Standard, OAIC Privacy Principles, and Sydney or Melbourne cloud residency.
